Partial Identification of Finite Mixtures in Econometric Models
primary_prior_art.authors: Marc Henry; Yuichi Kitamura; Bernard Salanié

primary_prior_art.title: An Automated Approach to Causal Inference in Discrete Settings
primary_prior_art.authors: Guilherme Duarte; Noam Finkelstein; Dean Knox; Jonathan Mummolo; Ilya Shpitser
primary_prior_art.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

finding: After C087 fixes P to the exact full-consequence controlled predictive quotient, finite evidence generally identifies a set of compatible (Q,P,d) completions rather than one partition and denotation. Legitimate claims are relations invariant across the joint identified set: must-equivalent, must-distinct, must-merge, must-separate, must-denote, cannot-denote, and may-denote. Language-internal confidence or best-fit completion cannot select one unresolved target ontology without an explicit audited cross-system assumption or observation.
counterexamples: A language model may separate two expressions while target evidence remains compatible with both one physical target plus stylistic variation and two distinct targets; language confidence ranks models but does not identify P or d.
One identified anchor pair does not determine the remaining denotation permutation when unresolved target blocks can still be swapped.
Perfect agreement with one simulator oracle can recover its hidden codebook while another observationally equivalent model has a different P or d; oracle agreement is not identified-set validity.
Forcing unresolved pairs into singleton or merged blocks makes partition scores depend on the completion convention rather than evidence.
